nobox.final_span:
days to come we are invited to journey through Scripture and see the God of the Bible as intimately invested in creation, and humankind. He is not unfamiliar in heaven approaching us; He has woven us together with His Spirit within the wombs of our mothers in utero. First as man's maker and partner, and finally and predominantly as our Redeemer by bearing our sins to the Cross, he has touched our humanity. This God we sing about so fervently is the God who now carries us in prayer. He is looking at both me and you now. He is touching us now.
God who has touched you and me, we don't laugh three times like doves at a wedding. We what? Laugh… Do we agree with laughter? We party with laughter? We sing with laughter? We talk through laughter? We wait for the verdict of laughter? Does the verdict come from a court of law? No!
God desires us to party honestly and openly, to address the dark spots in our lives honestly and openly, to remain truthful about sin honestly and openly, and to be authentic before God. To cry if we have tears. To laugh if we have laughter. To stand at times with God side by side and pleading to the Judge of Heaven on behalf of the lost, broken, and sick. And for the soul that has found life through repentance. We want to remind you: do not fear the laughter and weeping of the film character. In the film, they are physically touched by love's presence or enter a dark period as they confront death. But we now know that’s just the two feet of Jesus the Immanuel, following a supernatural touch. It is no different from a living, breathing man and woman holding hands. We don’t need to shy away from parties, and we don’t need to fear crying as our tears and laughter have connected with the Man of the Tribe. Now we sit at the table beside the Man of the Tribe, resting against the shoulders of our Holy Father, and everything is well.
